newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX seen eyeing 2,800 point level this week.
newsitem.headline: German DAX seen eyeing 2,800 point level this week.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares, which jumped to new record levels on Wednesday, was expected to continue to soar and could now aim for the 2,800 point level, dealers said.
"We could make 2,800 points by the end of the week," said one dealer, "The sentiment is great and everyone is bullish."
Dealers said the DAX was shaping up perfectly for the biggest flotation in its history next week when shares in Deutsche Telekom are first traded.
The IBIS DAX, reflecting all-day computer trade in the DAX, was up 6.72 points, or 0.24 percent at 2,771.02.

The DAX had touched an intraday record high of 2,778.83 points in electronic trade after the end of floor dealings, but pared its gains somewhat after the release of U.S. October PPI data and stayed lower as Wall Street failed to make convincing early gains.

Dealers said many market players had been taken by surprise by the rapid climb of the DAX, expecting more of a consolidation, and were now being forced to buy. "Too many peple were not on board for the upward climb," said one trader.
On Thursday attention will turn to U.S. consumer price data and Bayerische Hypobank nine month figures.

Veba surprised the market by reporting a 25 percent climb in nine month net profit to 1,227 billion marks. The stock touched an all-time high of 88.70 marks, before paring gains to end IBIS dealings up 3.67 marks at 87.67 marks.
Meanwhile nine month figures releases by BASF AG were somewhat disappointing, dealers said, and the stock ended IBIS dealings down 86 pfennigs at 51.61 marks.
Daimler Benz AG reached a year-high of 99.50 marks in IBIS dealings, before paring gains to end up three marks at 99.10 marks.
